precepts.text: There is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.
precepts.point: I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.

note.label: Daily Bread for a Dying Man

precepts.why:
Christ says, “no man cometh unto the Father, but by me.” Paul says the same: “For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus.”

He is the life. There is one God and one mediator between God and men, and that mediator is the man Christ Jesus. Nobody else stands between us and the Father: not a priest, not a saint, not anybody else.

That is why he is the way, the truth and the life, the manna from heaven and the door. The flesh is dying, the mind forgets, and the inward man has to be renewed daily by the word. The only way that renewing reaches us from the Father is through the one mediator, the man Christ Jesus.

precepts.text: Pray for all in authority, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.
precepts.point: The same prayer belongs to us: pray for all that are in authority, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness, keeping the commandments until Christ returns.

note.label: Genesis 33: The Meeting With Esau

precepts.why:
“I exhort therefore, that, first of all, supplications, prayers, intercessions, and giving of thanks, be made for all men; For kings, and for all that are in authority; that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.”

The same prayer belongs to us. Jacob prayed for deliverance, and the Most High made his enemy to be at peace with him in that moment. We pray for all that are in authority, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness, keeping the commandments until Christ returns.

precepts.text: Women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety.
precepts.point: When daughters are left without watch, the land falls into whoredom and fills with wickedness; the state of the community today shows the fruit of neglecting this law.

note.label: Leviticus 19: Ye Shall Be Holy, for I the Lord Your God Am Holy

precepts.why:
Israel is teaching the sisters self-respect again with the scriptures on dress: “that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array.”

Letting a daughter dress immodestly, or letting a little girl wear makeup and grown attire, is one of the ways a father prostitutes his daughter. Modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety, is the standard.

precepts.text: I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man; for Adam was first formed, then Eve, and the woman being deceived was in the transgression.
precepts.point: A sister helping to build up other sisters new in the congregation is right, and the sisters bless the nation with real talents, raising the children in the commandments, and the aged women teaching the young women. But teaching and leading the nation is not the place the Most High set for her.

note.label: Numbers 27: The Daughters of Zelophehad and the Ordination of Joshua

precepts.why:
Moses asked for a man over the congregation, and Paul gives the order behind it. “Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection. But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence.”

The reason is from the beginning: “For Adam was first formed, then Eve. And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression.” The woman was made to be an help meet unto the man, not to rule over him; she is the weaker vessel.

A sister helping to build up other sisters new in the congregation is right, but teaching and leading the nation is not the place the Most High set for her.

precepts.text: The order did not change in the New Testament: the woman is to learn in silence with all subjection, not to teach nor to usurp authority over the man.
precepts.point: Verse 9 proves it: my heart is toward the governors of Israel, the leaders who offered themselves willingly among the people. Her heart was with the men who led; she was not ruling over them.

note.label: Judges 5: The Song of Deborah and Barak: A Willing People

precepts.why:
The order did not change in the New Testament: “Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection. But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence.”

So Deborah cannot be used to justify women leading men. She did not usurp authority over the man; she arose “a mother in Israel” and her heart was “toward the governors of Israel”, the men who led. The Most High set a man over the congregation in the wilderness, and Paul keeps that same order.

precepts.text: Women are to adorn themselves in modest apparel with shamefacedness and sobriety, the inward beauty and not the outward attire of the harlot.
precepts.point: So she caught him and kissed him, and with an impudent face said she had peace offerings and had paid her vows. This is the opposite of the modest apparel the sisters are taught.

note.label: Proverbs 7: The Adulteress Hunts for the Precious Soul

precepts.why:
“And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.” She does not go out with her head covered in a modest dress; she dresses in the clothing of a harlot, loud and stubborn, her feet not abiding in her house.

Paul gives the opposite, the way the sisters are taught: “In like manner also, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array”. Modest apparel with shamefacedness and sobriety is the inward beauty, and it is set against the outward attire of the harlot.

The woman in Proverbs 7 is everything 1 Timothy 2:9 tells the sisters not to be: the attire of an harlot on the outside, and subtil of heart and impudent of face on the inside.
